title: Browser-based 3D fab twin + open equipment catalog +MIMAC scheduling benchmark
gist: A forum post from the builder of SemiconFab, a browser-based 300mm fab digital twin with an open catalog of 121 OEM tools (only 7 fully verified) and the MIMAC-2026 synthetic scheduling benchmark; it asks fab engineers whether field-level provenance is useful. A small hobbyist-scale project with no market claims.

insights.claim: SemiconFab is a browser-based 300mm cleanroom twin built with Three.js, including AMHS, MES/SPC/YMS panels and fault scenarios, but the author describes it as teaching-grade visualization rather than an industrial twin.
insights.speaker: W
insights.so_what: Open teaching tools lower the barrier to fab-operations education but are not a commercial fab-software threat.
insights.quote: The twin is currently teaching-grade visualization, not an industrial twin

insights.claim: The open catalog covers 121 real OEM tools under a 7-layer JSON schema with per-field provenance tiers from vendor_confirmed to synthetic, yet only 7 records are fully verified and 114 are drafts awaiting dimensions.
insights.speaker: W
insights.so_what: Public data on fab equipment is scarce enough that even an open effort has verified under 6% of its records.
insights.quote: Only 7 records are fully verified so far; 114 are drafts awaiting dimensions

insights.claim: MIMAC-2026 is a synthetic fab-scheduling benchmark with 18 tool groups, 217 machines, dispatching, AMHS and PM tasks, FIFO/SPT/EDD/CR baselines and a runnable Python simulator.
insights.speaker: W
insights.so_what: A reproducible benchmark for fab scheduling research; relevant to fab-automation and AI-scheduling startups.

insights.claim: The author asks fab engineers whether field-level provenance is more useful than a smaller verified-only catalog, and which equipment data is hardest to find publicly.
insights.speaker: W
insights.so_what: Reveals public equipment data scarcity as a gap for digital-twin and fab-AI efforts.
insights.quote: what equipment data is hardest to find publicly?
